title: Isolated region surge quarantine and circuit sanity review
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-24 we observed a sustained SLO miss in a single EU region after a token-heavy traffic surge from a small set of customers. The control plane routed traffic primarily to the EU region due to sticky affinity; regional circuit breakers tripped asymmetrically and left the region in a degraded state while secondary regions failed to absorb traffic fully. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root causes, immediate mitigations, and concrete follow-up actions to reduce recurrence risk and improve graceful degradation across regions.
timeline: 2026-02-24T09:12Z - First elevated 95th/99th tail latency alarms for model serve in eu-west-1 (console alert).
2026-02-24T09:23Z - Circuit breaker for eu-west-1 entered 'open' state for high-CPU and queue-depth thresholds.
2026-02-24T09:30Z - Autoscale attempted to increase worker pools but hit cluster GPU allocation limits in the region.
2026-02-24T09:40Z - Control plane routing persisted affinity to eu-west-1 for a subset of sessions; partial failover did not trigger due to hysteresis and metric smoothing settings.

2026-02-24T10:05Z - Engineering applied emergency mitigation: manually adjusted circuit thresholds, temporarily increased cross-region failover weight to secondary regions, and enabled short-lived request shedding for token-heavy clients.
2026-02-24T11:12Z - SLOs returned to acceptable ranges after traffic redistribution and targeted shedding.
2026-02-25 - Post-incident debug and data collection; initial RCA confirmed multiple contributing factors.
root_causes: Circuit breaker hysteresis parameters were tuned for steady-state backpressure and did not account for a concentrated short-duration token surge, causing asymmetrical open states.
Region affinity logic allowed sticky sessions to remain routed to the impacted region despite capacity degradation; affinity timeouts were too long.
KV cache warmup policy was conservative; many requests missed hot-prefix cache which amplified per-token work and increased latency during the surge.
Autoscaler policies were constrained by cluster-level GPU quotas and could not immediately provision additional capacity in eu-west-1.
Lack of a per-tenant token-budgeting feature allowed a small number of clients to consume disproportionate token throughput during the window.
Telemetry lacked a clear early-warning signal correlating token-length distributions with queue depth at the per-region level.
Playbook fall-through: circuit breaker state change did not trigger automatic rebalancing due to a gap between CB events and routing policy re-evaluation cadence.
immediate_mitigations: Manually lowered affinity stickiness for impacted sessions to force fast cross-region failover.
Adjusted circuit breaker hysteresis to allow faster half-open trials for regional circuits.
Enabled emergency token-rate limits for identified high-volume clients for the incident window.
Triggered manual pre-warm of KV cache for hot prefixes identified in the request samples.
Coordinated with infra to temporarily increase EU region GPU reservations to allow autoscaler headroom.
action_items: (A1) Implement per-region dynamic CB thresholds: change from static hysteresis to workload-aware thresholds based on short-window queue growth metrics. Owner: Ravi. ETA: 2026-03-18.
(A2) Reduce affinity timeout to 30s for session routing and add a fast-path failover when per-region queue depth crosses high-water mark. Owner: Network Routing. ETA: 2026-03-10.
(A3) Add token-length distribution telemetry to the per-region dashboard and create an early-warning composite metric. Owner: Observability. ETA: 2026-03-05.

(A4) Build a small per-tenant token budgeting enforcement in the gateway to limit excessive single-client token bursts; start with a soft cap and phased enforcement. Owner: API Platform. ETA: 2026-04-01.
(A5) Introduce KV cache prefill routine before failover to target hot prefixes and reduce cold-KV penalties. Owner: Serving Runtime. ETA: 2026-03-22.
(A6) Adjust autoscaler quota handling: add a fast-queue scaling pathway and improved quota preemption rules for emergency windows. Owner: Infra. ETA: 2026-03-29.
(A7) Update runbook and playbooks: ensure CB open events trigger an immediate routing re-eval and document manual steps used during this incident. Owner: SRE. ETA: 2026-03-08.
(A8) Add chaos test: simulate single-region token-heavy surge and validate fast failover and KV cache warmup. Owner: Reliability Engineering. ETA: 2026-04-05.
(A9) Postmortem review and retro session with PM/Design/Eng to validate UX impact and communication playbooks. Owner: Ava. ETA: 2026-03-12.
(A10) Create a per-route synthetic that sends mixed token-length traffic from multiple regions to verify cross-region rebalancing under load. Owner: QA. ETA: 2026-03-19.
